The defendant Ng Shui-ting appeared in court this morning wearing a green Polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black mask. The charges allege that the defendant, on July 10 and August 17 respectively, allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog to enter the vicinity of YOHO Mall in Yuen Long without being controlled by a leash not exceeding two metres in length. He faces two counts of an offence relating to allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place.

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks for mention, with no objection to bail. Acting Principal Magistrate Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to October 29 for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, conviction for the offence of allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place carries a fine of HK$25,000 and imprisonment for three months.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department Yip Yin said yesterday that if the owner decides to surrender the dog to the government, the department will consider options including humane euthanasia; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the dog may be classified as a "known dangerous dog," and the court may order that the dog must wear a muzzle whenever it goes out in future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection group Mochi Rescue, told集誌社 that the owner has expressed regret over signing the abandonment document; he also said Mochi is willing to take in the dog and provide a trainer to rehabilitate it.
